claims.text: The investigated material is an additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 high-entropy alloy containing dual nanoprecipitation.
Environmental transmission electron microscopy can elucidate mechanistic aspects of high-temperature oxidation in the specified alloy.
In-situ X-ray diffraction can elucidate mechanistic aspects of high-temperature oxidation.
In-situ X-ray diffraction can identify time- and temperature-dependent phase formation or transformation during oxidation.
In-situ characterization can reveal elemental redistribution associated with oxidation.
The elemental redistribution during oxidation is associated specifically with nanoprecipitates in Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3.
Characterizing nanoprecipitates during oxidation will improve understanding of the relationship between nanoprecipitates and oxidation behavior.
Current characterization techniques have limitations that constrain understanding of oxidation behavior.
The exact mechanisms of elemental redistribution and oxidation may remain incompletely understood.
Elemental distribution, oxidation behavior, and microstructural evolution can be measured during an in-situ high-temperature oxidation experiment.
Failure to reveal significant changes in elemental distribution or oxidation behavior would falsify the hypothesis.
